title: Claude Code (repo)
summary: The public side of Claude Code: the officially bundled example plugins, the source of the hook-based mods built into the CLI binary, deployment templates for teams, and the GitHub automation that runs the repository itself, including answering @claude mentions with Claude Code. The CLI binary itself is closed-source and downloaded separately; this repo is the open surface around it.

nodes.label: Claude Code CLI
nodes.summary: The terminal agent binary end users install and run; its source is not in this repo.
nodes.details:
- Downloaded via curl install script, npm, Homebrew, or winget (npm is deprecated).
- Loads the four built-in mods on every session and any plugins the user has installed.
- This repo only publishes install docs for it, plus the source that gets compiled into it (mods) and extensions for it (plugins).

nodes.label: Built-in mods
nodes.summary: Hook-module source for the four features shipped compiled into every Claude Code binary.
nodes.details:
- A mod is a plugin whose behavior is one register(on, options) hooking the engine's events.
- Ships: sec-default (locks org policy away from user-installed plugins), diff (the /diff pane), telemetry ($.telemetry analytics noun), agents-md (AGENTS.md as project instructions).
- Tested in isolation with `claude plugin test`, against a mocked engine, not a real session.
- Early access API; not installable from a marketplace, only read from source here.

nodes.label: Security default
nodes.summary: Outermost gate keeping an org's managed hooks, settings and tool policy out of reach of user-installed plugins.
nodes.details:
- Seated outermost on a machine with managed settings, or by default for Team/Enterprise orgs, unless a managed `prependPlugins` setting overrides the order.
- Continues past the user tier on the org's classic hooks, prompt content and settings; refuses a user-tier `tool.register` outside an MCP allowlist; restores the org's own tools in `tool.list`.
- Holds a settings deny rule over a user-tier allow/ask on `tool.check`, and under its `allowManagedModsOnly` option refuses a user-tier hooks module at `plugin.register`.
- Adds no policy of its own — it only shields the org's existing policy from what the plugins tier could otherwise override.

nodes.label: Content pass-through
nodes.summary: Sends the organization's classic hooks, managed prompt content, and settings reads straight past the user tier.
nodes.details:
- Covers classic.*, prompt.section, prompt.context, prompt.compose, skill.prompt, attribution.text, and settings.read.
- Every one of these just calls next.to(e, 'append'), skipping the user tier.
- The engine only raises prompt.compose at all when some loaded plugin hooks it, so seating this plugin makes that chain run on every prompt.

nodes.label: Subject visibility guard
nodes.summary: Keeps an organization-provided tool, command, or agent subject out of a person's plugins' reach.
nodes.details:
- Covers tool.describe, command.describe, agent.offer, and agent.spawn.
- Decided purely by the event's pinned provider.tier, never by a settings read.
- A subject from prepend, append, or no provider continues past the user tier; one from user, builtin, or core passes through every tier.

nodes.label: MCP tool policy guard
nodes.summary: Refuses a plugin's tool registration and restores the organization's own MCP tool listing under its allowlist.
nodes.details:
- tool.register: a user-tier caller is refused by name while managed settings hold allowedMcpServers (set at all, empty included); prepend/append callers always continue.
- tool.list: merges the organization's managed-server tools, as the organization's own tiers listed them, with every other tool as the user tier left it.
- Fails open to the organization's own listing when policy can't be read or either listing refused.

nodes.label: Deny-rule holder
nodes.summary: Re-checks a loosened tool.check answer past the user tier so a named deny rule still wins.
nodes.details:
- Runs the tool.check chain once, then checks next.trace for any managed-tier link that a person's plugin's answer loosened.
- If so, and managed policy hasn't set allowModsToOverrideDenyRules, re-runs the dispatch with the user tier skipped.
- A deny from that second run that names its own rule replaces the chain's answer; the person is told once per plugin per session.
- A failed hook falls back to the last run it could read: a deny stands, an unloosened verdict stands, anything else is refused.

nodes.label: Plugin admission guard
nodes.summary: Refuses to load a person's hooks module when managed policy limits mods to the organization's own.
nodes.details:
- Only asked about plugin.register in the user tier; prepend, append, and builtin modules are never asked.
- Reads allowManagedModsOnly straight from $.settings.read({source:'policy'}), not through the shared memo.
- On unless absent or false, refuses the module by name before any of its hooks, tools, or commands join.
- Fails closed: an unreadable policy or a hook failure refuses the module too.

nodes.label: Policy memo
nodes.summary: Reads managed policy once and serves it to a burst of calls for half a second.
nodes.details:
- Wraps $.settings.read({source:'policy'}) so a burst of calls (many tool.list / tool.register / tool.check events) reads the setting once.
- A policy change takes up to 500ms to be seen.
- Used by the MCP tool-policy guard and the deny-rule holder; the plugin-admission guard reads policy directly instead.

nodes.label: Managed settings
nodes.summary: The organization's managed settings this plugin reads through the policy source but never writes.
nodes.details: Outside this repo's scope: the engine's settings store, reached here only through $.settings.read({source:'policy'}).

nodes.label: Organization admin
nodes.summary: Sets the managed options that turn each guard's behavior on.
nodes.details:
- allowManagedModsOnly: limits mods to the ones deployed through managed settings plus Claude Code's built-ins.
- allowModsToOverrideDenyRules: lets a person's plugins answer over a settings deny rule on tool.check.
- Can also place this plugin in managed prependPlugins to choose where it sits.

nodes.label: Installed plugin
nodes.summary: A hooks module a person installed, running in the user tier beneath the organization's.
nodes.details: Covers a plugin installed normally, one named with --plugin-dir, or one kept in a person's mods folder. Sits in the user tier, beneath the organization's prepend tier and above its append tier.

nodes.label: Claude Code user
nodes.summary: The person running Claude Code, whose settings and deny rules this plugin protects.

nodes.label: Diff pane
nodes.summary: The `/diff` command: shows the session's uncommitted changes beside the transcript, refreshed live.
nodes.details:
- Opens on the first edit if the terminal is wide enough, or via the `/diff` command; draws file-by-file hunks that refresh as Claude edits files, runs shell commands, or finishes a turn.
- A file's ask button rides its hunks into the next prompt, so Claude sees exactly what changed.
- By far the largest mod (821 files, 227 of them tests) — its own git-probing layer, diff parsing, and the pane's view layer are each substantial internals.

nodes.label: Hook registration
nodes.summary: Binds the engine's `$` into a plain Host at session.start and wires every event the pane reacts to.
nodes.details:
- Holds the pane's whole mutable state (open/closed, the pinned backend, timers, the armed ask) as closures, not a class.
- Registers handlers for session.start, ui.render (both PromptHint and Pane components), command.run (`/diff`, `/clear`, `/resume`), tool.call, prompt.submit, ui.close and ui.scroll.
- Fails soft: if `/diff` is already held by a built-in or an org policy, logs a message instead of throwing.

nodes.label: VCS backend
nodes.summary: Locates the git repository behind the session's directory and pins every later git call to it.
nodes.details:
- `backendOf` asks any other installed version-control probes first, then falls back to git — none are installed as published.
- The git backend resolves the repository root with one `rev-parse`, then runs every later command with `--git-dir`/`--work-tree` pinned to it, under a fetch timeout and the C locale.
- Reads the dirty-paths baseline once per pin, used to tell checkpoint-session edits apart from pre-existing changes.

nodes.label: git binary
nodes.summary: The git command line, run as a child process to read diffs, hunks, branch base and head state.

nodes.label: Pane state model
nodes.summary: The pane's view-model: which files changed, which is selected, loaded hunk bodies, totals, and the fullscreen/dock layout.
nodes.details: Pure transition functions (afterFetch, afterNewSession, headerTotalsOf, modeLabelOf, …) that register.ts calls to turn a git fetch or a UI event into the next model, never touching git or the engine itself.

nodes.label: Pane rendering
nodes.summary: Draws the docked sidebar list, the fullscreen dialog, or a narrow-terminal fallback line from the current pane state.
nodes.details:
- `paneView` picks docked vs. dialog vs. the too-narrow note; `sections` and `detail` draw the file rows, hunks and legend beneath it.
- `pane-actions` closes over register's mutable state to answer clicks (select file, scroll, toggle noise/pre-session, cycle base, choose source, toggle ask).

nodes.label: Ask bridge
nodes.summary: Lets the person arm one file's diff so it rides their very next prompt as context, then drops it.
nodes.details: Trims the diff text to fit the remaining prompt-context budget (`fittedAskTextOf`); if it doesn't fit, tells the person and disarms instead of silently truncating mid-hunk.

nodes.label: Usage telemetry
nodes.summary: Logs feature marks (read ok/failed, base switch, file asked) and the one-per-session panel-shown row.
nodes.details: Every call swallows a missing `$.telemetry` noun or a refused row, so a telemetry outage never breaks the pane.

nodes.label: Edit & turn tracking
nodes.summary: Classifies tool calls as landed edits or writes, and groups a turn's edits for the per-turn diff view.
nodes.details: `mayHaveWritten` treats a shell call as a write unless the engine marked it read-only (e.g. `git status`); a landed main-loop edit is what triggers the pane's first-edit auto-open.

nodes.label: Command & text constants
nodes.summary: The static `/diff` CommandSpec, the pane's id/title, and the user-facing status strings the other parts reuse.

nodes.label: Developer
nodes.summary: The person running Claude Code who presses `/diff`, edits files, and reads or dismisses the diff pane.

edges.label: pins the repo on first use
registration can be blocked by policy

toggleAsk arms that file's path and diff text, and shows a status hint.
Submits the next prompt.
The fitted diff text is appended to that prompt's context, then the file disarms.
Marks the diff_selection_attach feature once the prompt carried it.

nodes.label: Telemetry noun
nodes.summary: Adds the `$.telemetry` noun other built-in mods call to log usage as first-party analytics rows.
nodes.details:
- Hooks `telemetry.log` and `telemetry.mark`; since no other mod seats this noun, its `engine.create` hook adds `$.telemetry` itself.
- Gates `telemetry.*` so a session with no provider throws naming the noun, and refuses calls from user-installed plugins — only built-in mods may log.
- Queues rows over `$.session`, `$.env`, `$.settings`, `$.fs`, `$.process`, `$.clock` and `$.http`, and sends them out in batches.
- Sends nothing wherever the CLI's own analytics are off.

nodes.label: Built-in callers
nodes.summary: The other CLI-bundled mods that call $.telemetry.log and .mark to record events and feature outcomes.
nodes.details:
- Only plugins seated in the builtin or core tier may call the noun; a person-installed or admin-listed plugin is refused by the gate.
- An entry whose `to` is 'collector' bypasses this mod entirely and rides whatever telemetry collector an operator configured, untouched.

nodes.label: Access gate
nodes.summary: Guards every telemetry.* call: lets builtin/core callers through, refuses anyone else, and catches a gate that throws.
nodes.details:
- SERVED_TIERS is just ['builtin', 'core'] — hardcoded, not configurable per build.
- The host stamps every call with the plugin that raised it (`next.origin`), and the gate reads its tier; no origin at all is a bug, so it throws rather than refusing silently.
- The `.catch` half replays beneath's own answer if it was actually invoked before throwing, so a real refusal (a malformed entry) still surfaces instead of being masked by REFUSED.

nodes.label: Hook registration
nodes.summary: The plugin's one entry point: wires the gate, the log/mark handlers, session.start/end, and the engine.create step that builds the sender.
nodes.details:
- engine.create adds `$.telemetry` only on an engine that has none of its own; where one already exists, this mod's own noun still stands (spread first), not replaced.
- session.start just remembers whether a person is at the prompt, read later by every batch as `is_interactive`.
- session.end awaits the sender's flush so queued rows aren't lost at process exit.

nodes.label: Entry validation
nodes.summary: Checks a log or mark entry's shape before it is ever queued: snake_case tokens, Choice-typed props, and mark's kind/reason rules.
nodes.details:
- A property value is a finite number, a boolean, or a Choice (a value plus the closed list it's drawn from); free text is refused outright.
- mark requires a reason on 'sad' and 'bad' and refuses one on 'ok'.
- Nothing free-form reaches a row — this is the only gate between the caller's argument and the wire; a refusal here rejects the caller's promise naming what was wrong.

nodes.label: Batch sender
nodes.summary: Queues checked rows and sends them in batches: on a timer, when 100 wait, or when the session ends.
nodes.details:
- Each batch re-reads the off-switches fresh, so a session that moves to a third-party provider or gateway mid-run sends nothing more.
- No first-party credential, or an ingest that still refuses after one retry, drops the batch; either outcome is one line in the debug log, never an error back to the caller.
- Session context is gathered once, lazily on the first queued row, and reused for every batch after.

nodes.label: Analytics off-switch
nodes.summary: Reads environment variables and the managed policy to decide, fresh on every batch, whether anything may be sent at all.
nodes.details:
- Off under test, DISABLE_TELEMETRY, the nonessential-traffic switch, or DO_NOT_TRACK.
- Off on a third-party provider (Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, and kin) the host doesn't itself manage.
- Off on a login gateway (the env switch or either of the two managed-settings policy pins) and on any deployment with its own custom OAuth URL.
- When the switches themselves can't be read, nothing is sent either.

nodes.label: Session context
nodes.summary: Gathers, once per session, everything every row carries in common: identity, session fields, the env block, and the repo's remote hash.
nodes.details:
- Identity comes from the CLI's own global config: the install's device id and the signed-in account's ids.
- The env block is built from one `uname`-style probe plus reads of terminal, shell, package manager, CI/GitHub Actions, VCS, Linux distro and WSL signals — all closed-list values, never a raw secret-shaped variable.
- Columns only the engine itself knows (its runtime version, memory, request betas, subscription tier) are never populated here and stay empty.

nodes.label: Anthropic event ingest
nodes.summary: The first-party event-logging endpoint — the same address the CLI's own analytics exporter posts its batches to.
nodes.details:
- Fixed URL (api.anthropic.com/api/event_logging/v2/batch), not read from session config, so a session on a different API base simply never reaches it.
- Authorized with the session's own resolved credential; a session with none never attempts to send.

flows.name: What happens when a built-in mod logs an event or marks a feature
flows.summary: A built-in-tier caller queues one row, which is validated, batched, and sent to Anthropic's ingest.

steps.text: A bundled mod calls $.telemetry.log({event, props}) or .mark({feature, kind}).
Gate confirms the caller's origin tier is builtin or core and lets the call through.
Event/feature name, kind, and every prop are checked as snake_case tokens or Choices; a bad entry rejects the caller's promise instead of being queued.
Checked row is queued; the batch flushes at 100 rows, after a short timer, or at session end.
Just before sending, the off-switches and managed policy are re-read; any one tripped drops the batch.
Session context (identity, env block, remote hash) is gathered once and reused for every batch after.
Batch POSTs with the session's own credential; one retry on a timeout, rate limit, or server error, else the batch is dropped.

flows.name: What happens when the session ends
flows.summary: Whatever rows are still queued go out in one last batch before the process exits.

steps.text: The host fires the session.end hook event.
register's session.end handler awaits the sender's flush.
Flush re-checks the off-switches before sending anything.
Remaining queued rows go out in one final POST.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md instructions
nodes.summary: Loads AGENTS.md files as project instructions, framed exactly like CLAUDE.md, by a configurable option.
nodes.details:
- Default mode (`claude-md-or-agents-md`): a project with no CLAUDE.md of its own gets its AGENTS.md files instead, walked from the filesystem root down via `$.fs.ancestors`.
- `claude-md-and-agents-md` loads every AGENTS.md beside CLAUDE.md (skipping a file CLAUDE.md already imports or links to); `managed-only` drops the project's and person's own files, keeping only the org's managed ones; `claude-md` disables it entirely.
- A `prompt.context` hook hands the engine the ancestor files as instruction files; a `tool.call` hook on `Read` attaches nested AGENTS.md the same way the engine attaches a nested CLAUDE.md.
- Every mode logs a usage row through `$.telemetry` where that noun is seated.

nodes.label: Hook registration
nodes.summary: Reads the resolved mode and wires the plugin's four event handlers, holding the per-loop state they share.
nodes.details:
- Returns immediately under `claude-md` (nothing but the usage row) and registers only a filtering `prompt.context` handler under `managed-only`.
- Otherwise keeps a `given` map of which AGENTS.md paths have already reached each agent loop, the last project root seen, and whether the project has its own CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Mode resolution
nodes.summary: Settles on one of the four instructionFiles modes, honouring a still-stored legacy option key for now.
nodes.details:
- Reads `instructionFiles` (claude-md / claude-md-or-agents-md / claude-md-and-agents-md / managed-only), defaulting to claude-md-or-agents-md.
- Falls back to a stored `projectInstructions` value only when instructionFiles was never set, mapping its old four values across; tells the user once in the transcript either way.

nodes.label: Session start report
nodes.summary: On every session.start, logs the active mode and tells the user once if the old option key is still in play.

nodes.label: Context injection
nodes.summary: On prompt.context, walks the filesystem for AGENTS.md files (or drops files under managed-only) and hands the engine the set to render as project instructions.
nodes.details:
- Under the fallback mode, first checks whether the project already has a CLAUDE.md on the walk; if so, adds nothing and leaves it to the engine.
- Skips any file the engine already holds by path or content, places each file's own `@` imports right after it, and logs a one-time debug line naming what loaded.
- Under managed-only, instead filters the handed instruction files down to managed and memory kinds only.

nodes.label: Nested file attach
nodes.summary: On a Read tool call, attaches the AGENTS.md of each directory between the project root and the file being read, once per loop and conversation.
nodes.details:
- Only runs where the engine would attach a nested CLAUDE.md too: skipped under --bare / CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ATTACHMENTS.
- Re-checks the project root on every call (follows /cd and worktree moves) and resets its sent-file tracking when the root changes.
- A subdirectory's AGENTS.md is dropped if a CLAUDE.md of that same directory claims it instead.

nodes.label: Fork inheritance
nodes.summary: On agent.spawn with fork:true, copies the parent loop's already-sent file set to the new forked agent so it isn't attached twice.
nodes.details: A plain /fork or /subtask (not an Agent-tool fork) raises no agent.spawn event and simply starts from an empty sent-file set.

nodes.label: Path & frame rules
nodes.summary: Decides which files are below the project root, resolves ~ paths, and tells an AGENTS.md apart from the CLAUDE.md names it must defer to.
nodes.details:
- Compares paths by normalized spelling (handles Windows separators) rather than resolving symlinked aliases.
- Supplies the AGENTS.md / .claude/AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md name lists the filesystem walk searches for.

nodes.label: Usage rows
nodes.summary: Builds the mode, load, and nested-attach count rows (and the ok/sad mark) this plugin reports, with no paths or file text.

nodes.label: Engine filesystem API
nodes.summary: The engine's $.fs.ancestors, $.session.root/cwd, and $.env.get calls this plugin relies on to find instruction files and know where it is running.
nodes.details: Finds nothing on a thin client whose workspace files are remote, same as the engine's own walk.

filters to files below the root

flows.name: What happens when Claude reads a file in a subdirectory
flows.summary: The Read hook attaches that directory's AGENTS.md the way the engine attaches a nested CLAUDE.md.

steps.text: A Read tool call lands on a file under the project root.
Walks the directories strictly between the root and the file for AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Engine type contract
nodes.summary: Shared TypeScript declarations for every hook event and `$` noun the engine exposes to mods.
nodes.details:
- One generated file (`types/claude-code.d.ts`), written by Claude Code's own `/plugin-types` command, that every mod's `tsconfig.json` includes alongside the other mods' `types/*.d.ts`.
- Because a call like `$.telemetry.log(...)` types against telemetry's real contract, an implementation cannot drift from what callers read.
- A mod that adds a noun (only telemetry does) declares it here via its own `types/index.d.ts`, never duplicated elsewhere.

refuses telemetry calls from installed plugins

flows.name: What happens when a managed session starts
flows.summary: sec-default seats outermost, then agents-md decides the session's instructions and logs the choice.

steps.text: On a managed machine, loads outermost before any other mod or plugin, holding the org's hook/settings/tool policy out of reach.
Decides which instruction files apply (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or managed-only) and hands them to the engine as the session's project instructions.
Logs which mode loaded and how many files, via $.telemetry.log and $.telemetry.mark.

flows.name: What happens when a plugin tries to grant itself a new tool
flows.summary: sec-default's policy wins over whatever the plugin or user tier asks for.

steps.text: Sits outermost in the hook chain, seeing every plugin.register and tool.register call before the engine does.
Refuses a user-tier tool.register outside the org's MCP allowlist and restores the org's own tool list, regardless of what the plugin requested.

nodes.label: Official plugins
nodes.summary: Example plugins (commands, agents, skills, hooks) anyone can install into their own Claude Code.
nodes.details:
- Installed via /plugin, from this repo or a marketplace, not built into the binary.
- Covers plugin authoring (plugin-dev), git workflow (commit-commands), PR review, hookify's custom-hook generator, the ralph-wiggum iteration loop, and more.

nodes.label: Git workflow commands
nodes.summary: Slash commands that wrap git add/commit, push, and PR creation into one step.
nodes.details:
- /commit stages and commits with a generated message.
- /commit-push-pr commits, pushes, and opens a PR in one call.
- /clean_gone removes local branches and worktrees whose remote was deleted.

nodes.label: PR review agents
nodes.summary: Runs several specialized agents over a pull request and scores findings by confidence to cut false positives.
nodes.details:
- code-review runs 5 parallel agents (CLAUDE.md compliance, bugs, history, PR history, comments).
- pr-review-toolkit adds comment-analyzer, pr-test-analyzer, silent-failure-hunter, type-design-analyzer, code-reviewer, code-simplifier.
- Both are invoked from a review-pr style slash command.

nodes.label: Feature dev workflow
nodes.summary: A structured, multi-phase command that explores the codebase, designs an architecture, then reviews the result.
nodes.details:
- code-explorer traces execution paths and documents existing patterns.
- code-architect produces an implementation blueprint from those patterns.
- code-reviewer checks the finished change for bugs and convention drift.

nodes.label: Plugin dev kit
nodes.summary: An 8-phase guided workflow plus seven reference skills for building, validating, and publishing new Claude Code plugins.
nodes.details:
- /plugin-dev:create-plugin walks through component design and implementation.
- Skills cover hooks, MCP integration, plugin structure, settings, commands, agents, and skill-writing itself.
- agent-creator and skill-reviewer draft and critique new agents/skills; plugin-validator checks plugin.json and file layout.

nodes.label: Plugin developer
nodes.summary: The person building a new Claude Code plugin, who drives the workflow and answers its clarifying questions.

nodes.label: Create-plugin command
nodes.summary: The /plugin-dev:create-plugin slash command: an 8-phase guided workflow from discovery to documentation.
nodes.details:
- Phases: discovery, component planning, detailed design, structure creation, component implementation, validation, testing, documentation.
- Asks clarifying questions instead of assuming, and tracks progress with TodoWrite.
- Loads the reference skills and dispatches the three agents as each phase needs them.

nodes.label: Reference skills
nodes.summary: Seven on-demand skills covering plugin structure, hooks, MCP, settings, commands, agents, and skill authoring.
nodes.details:
- Each loads only when its trigger phrases match, keeping context lean (progressive disclosure).
- plugin-structure covers the manifest and directory layout; hook-development and mcp-integration cover event automation and external integrations; plugin-settings covers .local.md config; command-development, agent-development, and skill-development cover each component type's file format and best practices.

nodes.label: Agent creator
nodes.summary: AI-assisted agent that turns a plain description into a complete, tuned agent markdown file.
nodes.details:
- Uses Claude Code's own proven agent-generation system prompt.
- Only has Write and Read tools: it drafts the agent file directly, it doesn't explore the repo.

nodes.label: Plugin validator
nodes.summary: Checks a plugin's manifest and directory structure for correctness, triggered explicitly or right after components are created.

nodes.label: Skill reviewer
nodes.summary: Reviews a newly written or edited skill for trigger strength and structure, against skill-development's best practices.

nodes.label: Validation scripts
nodes.summary: Shell scripts the validator agents shell out to: schema checks, a hook test harness, a linter, and frontmatter parsing.

nodes.label: New plugin files
nodes.summary: The plugin directory being created on disk: manifest, commands, agents, skills, and hooks for the developer's own plugin.

flows.name: What happens when a developer builds a new plugin
flows.summary: The guided command walks discovery through documentation, delegating generation and validation to the reference skills and agents.

steps.text: Developer runs the command, optionally with a plugin description.
Command loads plugin-structure (and others as needed) to plan components.
For each needed agent, the command hands off to agent-creator.
Agent-creator writes the tuned agent markdown file.
Command itself writes the manifest, commands, hooks, and skill files.
Command runs the validation phase over the finished plugin.
Validator shells out to validate-hook-schema.sh, validate-agent.sh, etc.
Validator reports any structural or manifest problems to fix before publishing.

flows.name: What happens when a skill gets reviewed
flows.summary: The skill-reviewer agent checks a skill's triggers and structure against the skill-development skill's own standards.

steps.text: Developer asks for a review after writing or editing a skill.
Reviewer checks the skill against skill-development's progressive-disclosure and trigger-phrase guidance.
Reviewer reports weak triggers or structural gaps to fix.

nodes.label: Hookify
nodes.summary: Lets Claude write its own PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop/UserPromptSubmit hooks from a plain-language rule or a conversation it analyzes.
nodes.details:
- conversation-analyzer reads a transcript for behaviors worth preventing.
- writing-rules explains hook-rule syntax; a rule engine (core/) evaluates rules at each hook event.
- /hookify, /hookify:list, /hookify:configure, /hookify:help manage the installed rules.

nodes.label: Create rule command
nodes.summary: The /hookify slash command: turns a plain-language instruction or a scan of the conversation into a new hook rule.
nodes.details:
- With arguments, uses the text directly plus a quick look at the last 10-15 messages for examples.
- With no arguments, delegates to the conversation-analyzer agent instead.
- Asks the user which findings to turn into rules, block vs warn, and what pattern to match, then writes the rule file.

nodes.label: Conversation analyzer
nodes.summary: Reads recent user messages and finds corrections, frustration, or repeated issues worth turning into a hook.
nodes.details:
- Looks for explicit "don't do X" requests, reverted actions, and repeated mistakes.
- Converts each finding into a tool name, a candidate regex pattern, and a severity (high/medium/low).
- Explicitly told to ignore hypotheticals and one-time already-fixed accidents.

nodes.label: Writing-rules skill
nodes.summary: Reference skill every hookify command loads first to get the rule file's frontmatter and pattern syntax right.

nodes.label: List & configure commands
nodes.summary: The /hookify:list and /hookify:configure commands: show existing rules and toggle them on or off.
nodes.details:
- list reads every rule file's frontmatter and prints a table (name, enabled, event, pattern).
- configure lets the user pick rules via AskUserQuestion, then edits enabled: true/false in place.

nodes.label: Rule files
nodes.summary: User-authored .claude/hookify.<name>.local.md files in the current project; the actual configuration.
nodes.details:
- Live in the project's own .claude/ folder, not in this plugin's repo.
- Each file is YAML frontmatter (name, enabled, event, pattern or conditions, action) plus a markdown message body.
- Meant to be git-ignored; take effect immediately, no restart.

nodes.label: Example rules
nodes.summary: Shipped sample .local.md files (dangerous rm, console.log, sensitive files, require-tests) users copy from.

nodes.label: Rule loader
nodes.summary: Globs the project's .claude/hookify.*.local.md files and parses each into a Rule/Condition object.

nodes.label: Rule engine
nodes.summary: Compiles each rule's regex (cached) and checks it against the current tool call, combining warn/block results.
nodes.details: Blocking matches take priority over warning matches; all matching messages get combined into one response.

nodes.label: Hook executors
nodes.summary: Four scripts wired into hooks.json that Claude Code itself invokes on PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, and UserPromptSubmit.
nodes.details:
- Each script reads the tool-call JSON from stdin, maps tool name to an event type (bash/file/stop/prompt), and asks the rule engine to evaluate it.
- Import failures are swallowed into a systemMessage so a broken rule file never blocks Claude Code itself.

flows.name: What happens when a user runs /hookify
flows.summary: A plain-language complaint turns into an active rule file in one command.

steps.text: User runs /hookify, with or without a specific instruction
If no instruction given, hands off recent messages to find frustration/correction signals
Returns candidate patterns with severity and suggested rule names
Loads the correct frontmatter/pattern syntax before writing anything
Writes the confirmed rule as a new .claude/hookify.<name>.local.md file

flows.name: What happens on the next tool call
flows.summary: Every Bash, Edit, Write, or Stop in the session gets checked against the rule files before Claude Code proceeds.

steps.text: Claude Code fires the matching hook (e.g. PreToolUse) before the tool runs
Asks for every enabled rule whose event matches this tool
Globs and parses the project's current .local.md files fresh each time
Passes the tool's input data in for evaluation
Returns a combined warn/block decision, which Claude Code surfaces or enforces

flows.name: What happens when a user lists or toggles rules
flows.summary: Rules can be reviewed and switched on/off without ever leaving the chat.

steps.text: User runs /hookify:list or /hookify:configure
Reads every rule file's frontmatter to show current name/event/enabled state
On configure, edits enabled: true/false directly in the chosen file

nodes.label: Security review hook
nodes.summary: A PreToolUse hook that scans edits for 9 risky patterns (injection, XSS, eval, pickle, os.system, etc.) and warns Claude.
nodes.details:
- security_reminder_hook.py is the entry point; patterns.py holds the regex checks.
- llm.py adds an LLM-based second pass for subtler issues.
- gitutil.py/diffstate.py scope the check to the current diff; session_state.py avoids repeat warnings.

nodes.label: Agent SDK dev kit
nodes.summary: Scaffolds a new Claude Agent SDK project and verifies a Python or TypeScript one follows SDK best practices.
nodes.details:
- /new-sdk-app sets up a fresh Agent SDK application.
- agent-sdk-verifier-py and agent-sdk-verifier-ts check an existing app's config and docs against SDK conventions.

nodes.label: Standalone skills
nodes.summary: Two auto-invoked skills with no commands or hooks: migrating prompts/code to Opus 4.5, and frontend visual-design guidance.
nodes.details:
- claude-opus-4-5-migration rewrites model strings, beta headers, and prompt phrasing for the newer model.
- frontend-design triggers on UI work and pushes toward distinctive layouts/typography instead of generic AI aesthetics.

nodes.label: Session output styles
nodes.summary: Two SessionStart hooks that recreate output styles no longer built into Claude Code: explanatory asides and a learning mode.
nodes.details:
- explanatory-output-style injects educational context about implementation choices at session start.
- learning-output-style does the same plus asks the user to write small (5-10 line) code contributions at decision points.

nodes.label: Ralph Wiggum loop
nodes.summary: A Stop hook that refuses to let the session end while a loop is active, feeding Claude's last output back in to keep iterating.
nodes.details:
- /ralph-loop starts the loop (setup-ralph-loop.sh writes a state file); /cancel-ralph ends it.
- stop-hook.sh intercepts the session's exit attempt and re-prompts Claude with its own prior output.

edges.label: calls Claude API to analyze diff

flows.name: What happens when Claude edits a risky file
flows.summary: The security plugin catches risky patterns before a write lands and can escalate to an LLM check.

steps.text: PreToolUse intercepts the Edit/Write call before it executes.
Regex patterns scan the diff for the 9 known risk patterns.
For subtler cases, llm.py sends the diff to the Claude API for a second opinion.
A warning surfaces in the session if something looks risky; session_state.py avoids repeating it.

flows.name: What happens when someone builds a new plugin
flows.summary: plugin-dev's guided workflow turns an idea into an installable plugin.

steps.text: Runs /plugin-dev:create-plugin to start the 8-phase build.
Skills guide the user through hooks, commands, skills, MCP config, and settings.
plugin-validator checks the result, then it installs like any other plugin.

flows.name: What happens during a Ralph Wiggum loop
flows.summary: The Stop hook keeps feeding Claude's own output back in until the task is done.

steps.text: Starts the loop with /ralph-loop; setup-ralph-loop.sh writes a state file.
stop-hook.sh intercepts the session's exit attempt.
Claude's last output is fed back in as the next prompt, and the cycle repeats until /cancel-ralph or completion.

nodes.label: Deployment examples
nodes.summary: Templates for rolling Claude Code out to a team: MDM profiles, settings policy, and a self-hosted API gateway.
nodes.details:
- MDM templates for Jamf/Kandji/Intune/Group Policy deploy managed-settings.json to a fleet.
- Settings templates (lax/strict/bash-sandbox) restrict permissions, hooks, and tools org-wide.
- Gateway examples (AWS/GCP Terraform + setup scripts) stand up a reverse proxy in front of the Claude API.
- Community-maintained starting points, not supported configs.

nodes.label: MDM deployment templates
nodes.summary: Per-platform wrappers (Jamf, Kandji, Intune, Group Policy) that push the same managed-settings.json policy fleet-wide.
nodes.details:
- All templates encode the same minimal example key (permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode).
- Community-maintained; the README warns they may be unsupported or incorrect.
- Settings deployed this way sit at the top of the precedence order and cannot be overridden by users.

nodes.label: macOS MDM payloads
nodes.summary: Custom Settings plist for Jamf/Kandji, plus a full .mobileconfig profile for local testing.

nodes.label: Windows MDM payloads
nodes.summary: PowerShell script for Intune platform scripts, plus ADMX/ADML templates for Group Policy or Intune ADMX import.

nodes.label: Platform-neutral base policy
nodes.summary: The one managed-settings.json any MDM can drop straight into the system config directory.

nodes.label: Settings file examples
nodes.summary: Three ready-made settings.json variants (lax, strict, bash-sandbox) for organization-wide rollout.
nodes.details:
- Differ in which precedence-only keys they set: blocking marketplaces, hooks, bash approval, or running Bash inside a sandbox.
- Meant to be merged or used as managed-settings.json / settings.json / settings.local.json starting points.

nodes.label: Gateway on AWS
nodes.summary: Reference deployment for a self-hosted Claude apps gateway on AWS, fronting Amazon Bedrock.
nodes.details:
- setup.sh scripts the walkthrough end to end via the aws CLI: security groups, IAM roles, an ECR image with gateway.yaml baked in, RDS for Postgres, Secrets Manager, and an ECS Fargate service behind an internal ALB.
- terraform/ provisions the same architecture as code (two-pass apply).
- Idempotent and reuse-by-name aware; posture drift is checked and warned about, never silently adopted.
- Not covered: the EKS track, console-only Bedrock model access, and client MDM push (that's the mdm-templates node).

nodes.label: Gateway on GCP
nodes.summary: Reference deployment for the same self-hosted gateway on GCP, fronting Agent Platform (Vertex AI).
nodes.details:
- setup.sh scripts the walkthrough via gcloud: Cloud Run or GKE, Cloud SQL for Postgres, Secret Manager, service-account auth to Agent Platform.
- terraform/ is the IaC equivalent of setup.sh, same env-overridable defaults as the AWS track.

nodes.label: Bash validator hook example
nodes.summary: A sample PreToolUse hook that rewrites or blocks Bash commands before they run (e.g. grep to rg).
nodes.details: Installed by pointing a PreToolUse/Bash hook entry in settings at this script's path; matches commands against a small regex rule list and can rewrite the command or reject it with a message.

flows.name: What happens when an org rolls out managed settings
flows.summary: An admin starts from a settings template, wraps it for their MDM platform, and every install picks it up as the top-precedence config.

steps.text: Admin picks the lax, strict, or bash-sandbox template as a starting point
Wraps that JSON into a Jamf, Kandji, Intune, or Group Policy payload
MDM pushes it to managed-settings.json on each machine; the CLI reads it at startup as the top-precedence source

flows.name: What happens when a team stands up a self-hosted gateway
flows.summary: setup.sh or its Terraform equivalent provisions the gateway container behind a load balancer, pointed at the team's own cloud account.

steps.text: setup.sh (or terraform/) provisions ECS Fargate, RDS, and secrets on AWS, with gateway.yaml baked into the image
The equivalent track provisions Cloud Run and Cloud SQL on GCP
End users point their CLI at the internal gateway URL instead of api.anthropic.com

nodes.label: Repo automation
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflows and scripts that triage issues/PRs and answer @claude mentions on this repo, behind an egress firewall.
nodes.details:
- claude.yml runs the Claude Code action on @claude mentions, with --permission-mode auto so unlisted tool calls go through Claude's own safety review.
- Runs on GitHub's egress-firewall runner; .github/egress-firewall.yaml allow-lists every host a job may reach (Claude API, GitHub API, npm, apt).
- workflow-hardening.yml fails a workflow that calls Claude without the firewall runner or auto permission mode, unless it's named in an exemption table.
- Other workflows auto-close/dedupe/label-lifecycle issues via scripts/ (gh.sh is a locked-down gh CLI wrapper).

nodes.label: @claude responder
nodes.summary: Runs Claude Code when someone writes "@claude" in an issue, PR comment, or review, letting it reply or make edits.
nodes.details:
- Fires on issue_comment, pull_request_review_comment, issues (opened/assigned), and pull_request_review, gated on the comment/issue body containing "@claude".
- Authenticates to the Claude API via Workload Identity Federation (its GitHub OIDC token is exchanged for a short-lived API token) instead of a static key.
- The action's own default for @claude mentions is --permission-mode acceptEdits; this workflow's claude_args overrides it to --permission-mode auto, so anything outside the allowed tools still needs Claude Code's own safety review.

nodes.label: Issue triage
nodes.summary: Runs Claude Code on every new issue or comment to judge if it's about Claude Code and relabel it through a restricted tool.
nodes.details:
- Triggered on issues opened and on non-bot issue_comment created; cancels an in-progress run for the same issue.
- Its prompt (.claude/commands/triage-issue.md) may only read labels/issues through scripts/gh.sh and apply changes through scripts/edit-issue-labels.sh, and is told never to post a comment.
- claude_args disallows Write/Edit/WebFetch/WebSearch and forces claude-opus-4-6, the minimum model that runs the --permission-mode auto safety review.

nodes.label: Duplicate finder
nodes.summary: Runs Claude Code on every new issue to search for likely duplicates and post up to 3 matches as one comment.
nodes.details:
- Its prompt (.claude/commands/dedupe.md) fans out into sub-agents: one checks whether dedupe is even needed, one summarizes the issue, five search in parallel with diverse keywords, one filters false positives.
- May only read through scripts/gh.sh and write through scripts/comment-on-duplicates.sh; claude_args disallows file-editing and web tools.
- A second workflow step logs a "duplicate comment added" event to Statsig after the job runs (skipped silently if no API key is configured).

nodes.label: Restricted GH scripts
nodes.summary: The only way the triage and dedupe agents may touch GitHub: wrapper scripts that whitelist specific reads and the one write each agent needs.
nodes.details:
- gh.sh allows only `issue view`, `issue list`, `search issues`, `label list` and a few flags, and blocks repo:/org:/user: search qualifiers.
- edit-issue-labels.sh and comment-on-duplicates.sh read the target issue number from the triggering GitHub event payload, not from an argument, and silently drop any label/issue that doesn't already exist.

nodes.label: Lifecycle rule table
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for the issue lifecycle labels, their timeout in days, and their nudge message.
nodes.details: Five labels in order: invalid (3d), needs-repro (7d), needs-info (7d), stale (14d), autoclose (14d). Also sets the upvote threshold that exempts a popular issue from going stale.

nodes.label: Issue lifecycle sweeper
nodes.summary: Scheduled escalation through the lifecycle labels, a nudge comment on each new label, and a reset the moment someone replies.

nodes.label: Sweep (cron)
nodes.summary: Runs at 10:00 and 22:00 UTC; walks open issues and applies the next lifecycle label or closes ones past the autoclose timeout.

nodes.label: Nudge comment
nodes.summary: Fires whenever a lifecycle label is applied; posts the matching nudge message so the author gets a heads-up before the next step.

nodes.label: Un-stick on reply
nodes.summary: Strips the autoclose label the moment a non-bot comment lands on a labeled issue, cancelling the pending close.

nodes.label: Duplicate auto-close
nodes.summary: Closes an issue 3 days after the duplicate finder's comment if nobody objected, plus a manual backfill for old issues that never got one.

nodes.label: Auto-close (cron)
nodes.summary: Runs daily at 09:00 UTC; finds issues whose duplicate-finder comment is older than 3 days with no new comment or 👎, and closes them.

nodes.label: Backfill detection
nodes.summary: Manually-triggered job that re-runs duplicate detection on old issues closed without ever getting a duplicate comment; supports dry-run.

nodes.label: CI guardrails
nodes.summary: PR checks that keep the automation safe: enforce the Claude-calling jobs' firewall settings, flag risky new permissions, and test the mod plugins.

nodes.label: Hardening check
nodes.summary: Fails a PR if a Claude-calling job skips the firewall runner or --permission-mode auto, or the allow-list is misconfigured.

nodes.label: Permission-risk flag
nodes.summary: Comments on a PR the first time it adds or edits allowed_non_write_users in a workflow file, since that lets non-write users trigger Claude.

nodes.label: Mod plugin tests
nodes.summary: Typechecks every mod's hooks and runs its test suite when mods/ changes.

edges.label: warns on a risky new permission

nodes.label: Telemetry & notify
nodes.summary: Side-channel logging and cross-repo notification triggered by issue events, separate from the agents' own work.
nodes.details: log-issue-events.yml logs every issue open/close to Statsig. issue-opened-dispatch.yml fires a repository_dispatch to a separate repo on issue open so it can react too, swallowing any failure.

nodes.label: Egress firewall allow-list
nodes.summary: The host allow-list the three Claude-calling jobs are restricted to when they run on GitHub's firewalled runner.
nodes.details: Allows api.anthropic.com, api.github.com, claude.ai, downloads.claude.ai, the bun/npm/apt mirrors the Claude Code action needs, and events.statsigapi.net. mode: enforce blocks everything else.

edges.label: asks Claude API to analyze and reply

allows calls to Claude + GitHub APIs
closes issues after its unanswered comment

flows.name: What happens when someone writes @claude
flows.summary: A comment, review, or issue containing "@claude" triggers Claude Code to read the thread and respond, inside the firewalled runner.

steps.text: Posts a comment, review, or opens an issue containing "@claude".
GitHub Actions starts the job on the egress-firewall runner and exchanges its OIDC token for a short-lived Claude API token.
Its outbound calls are capped to the allowed hosts.
Claude Code reads the thread and posts a reply or edit, with --permission-mode auto backing any out-of-scope tool call.

flows.name: What happens when a new issue is opened
flows.summary: A freshly opened issue is triaged for labels and checked for duplicates at the same time, both through the same restricted GitHub scripts.

steps.text: Opens a new issue.
Claude Code reads the issue and label list only through gh.sh, then applies labels through edit-issue-labels.sh.
All reads and label edits are routed through the whitelisted scripts.
The same "issues opened" event also starts the duplicate finder.
Five parallel search agents look for duplicates; surviving matches get one comment linking up to 3 issues.
If nobody objects within 3 days, the daily sweep closes the issue as a duplicate.

flows.name: What happens when an issue goes quiet
flows.summary: An inactive issue is escalated through labels on a timer and nudged at each step, unless a reply resets the clock.

steps.text: Twice a day the sweep checks every open issue's current label against its timeout, and a nested job posts a nudge comment whenever a label is newly applied.
Looks up each label's timeout in days and its nudge message.
A reply at any point strips the autoclose label and resets the clock.

nodes.label: Anthropic maintainer
nodes.summary: Writes and reviews the mods, plugins, examples, and workflow code, and merges PRs.

nodes.label: Claude Code user
nodes.summary: Installs the CLI and, optionally, plugins and fleet-wide settings from this repo.

nodes.label: GitHub & Claude API
nodes.summary: GitHub fires the webhook events repo-automation reacts to; the Claude API is what actually answers @claude.
nodes.details: Two distinct outside services sharing one node because both are used only by Repo automation: GitHub (issues, PRs, comments) as the event source and write target, and api.anthropic.com as the model repo-automation calls.
